Decision: Remove scroll-follow from playback in v1
Reason: Competing input systems (scroll, playback, click) created confusing UX and unnecessary complexity
Implication: Playback is now driven only by transport controls and text interaction
Author: MH

Decision: Add global mute button that does not affect playback
Reason: Users who can't or don't want to listen to audio but still want the rest of the story-theater playback experience now have that option readily available in the flow of the page at all times.
Implication: Playback and volume controlled separately if needed
Author: MH

Decision: Adopt playback-driven interaction model as primary UX
Reason: A single source of truth for progression simplifies mental model and reduces conflicting inputs
Implication: All timing highlighting and media behavior are tied to playback state rather than scroll position
Author: MH

Decision: Establish flow-first principle across desktop and mobile
Reason: User immersion and narrative continuity are core to READiscover’s value proposition
Implication: UI elements must not interrupt story flow unless explicitly triggered
Author: MH

Decision: Define margin media as ambient by default with optional inspection mode
Reason: Persistent interruptions would degrade reading and listening experience
Implication: Margin media appears without pausing playback and inspection pauses playback in overlay
Author: MH

Decision: Implement sentence-level click-to-seek for timed text
Reason: Direct manipulation improves usability and reinforces audio-text linkage
Implication: Users can click sentences to seek playback without requiring word-level sync yet
Author: MH

Decision: Use segment-level audio clips with optional clip boundaries
Reason: Single long audio file caused misalignment and poor segment control
Implication: Each segment can define audioStartTime and audioEndTime for precise transitions
Author: MH

Decision: Introduce floating playback controls as a revealable utility layer
Reason: Persistent controls obstructed content and margin media
Implication: Controls are hidden by default and accessed via launcher reducing clutter
Author: MH

Decision: Separate chart prototyping into standalone sandbox environment
Reason: Early integration would constrain experimentation and slow iteration
Implication: Charts can be evaluated independently before deciding placement in READiscover
Author: MH

Decision: Adopt publication-first strategy over immediate platform development
Reason: Limited resources and need to prove concept before scaling
Implication: Focus remains on flagship stories before building creator tools
Author: MH

Decision: Defer CMS and backend authoring tools until frontend experience is validated
Reason: Premature tooling would add complexity without validated workflow needs
Implication: Content creation remains manual for now and future CMS will be informed by usage
Author: MH

Decision: Prioritize manual timing alignment for demo phase
Reason: Automated alignment tools are not yet integrated and demo quality depends on precise sync
Implication: Manual cue editing is acceptable for V1 with future AI alignment possible
Author: MH

Decision: Standardize segment-based story architecture
Reason: Need for modular extensible storytelling system
Implication: All content types conform to segment model enabling timeline integration
Author: MH

Decision: Playback is the source of truth for READiscover progression
Reason: Scroll-driven playback and multiple competing inputs created confusing UX and system complexity
Implication: Text highlighting media cues and active segment state all follow playback rather than scroll
Author: MH

Decision: Adopt flow-first storytelling on both desktop and mobile
Reason: The story experience should remain primary and continuous rather than being interrupted by UI layers
Implication: Media and controls must support the story instead of dominating it
Author: MH

Decision: Inspection pauses playback but ambient media does not
Reason: Users need to explore context without the system interrupting them automatically
Implication: Media can appear alongside playback but deeper inspection becomes an intentional modal/context state
Author: MH

Decision: Use vertical two-stage mobile system instead of horizontal stage switching
Reason: Horizontal switching weakened conceptual clarity and risked breaking story flow on mobile
Implication: Mobile keeps the story as the default stage and uses a secondary companion stage for media
Author: MH

Decision: Treat section logos as section identity resting state rather than filler
Reason: Empty media stages felt awkward but adding many more charts was not feasible before launch
Implication: Hero state leads into default team identity state and media cues temporarily override that identity
Author: MH

Decision: Use atmospheric hero image only in opening frame
Reason: The opening needed more depth and scene-setting without adding another interactive layer
Implication: Arena photo serves as background atmosphere only and fades into the story rather than becoming content
Author: MH

Decision: Do not implement true line measurement before launch
Reason: Range.getClientRects based line tracking is powerful but too risky and time-intensive for deadline week
Implication: Use span-based or other launch-safe highlight refinement for MVP and defer physical line tracking until after launch
Author: MH

Decision: Enforce one dominant layer at a time across the UI
Reason: Story controls and media were all competing for visual authority especially on mobile
Implication: Story Mode Control Mode and Context Mode must each have a clear dominant surface and other layers must yield
Author: MH

Decision: Default playback UI to mini-bar first with expanded controls only on user intent
Reason: Full playback controls were taking too much screen space and overpowering story theater
Implication: Playback controls become temporary tools rather than a permanently dominant layer
Author: MH

Decision: Strengthen chart interaction affordance rather than adding many more charts
Reason: The issue was hierarchy and discoverability more than lack of media volume
Implication: Existing charts should invite interaction more clearly and inspect mode should feel more prominent
Author: MH

Decision: Deploy first to Hanson Hoops GitHub Pages subsite rather than waiting for readiscovermedia.com
Reason: The playoff preview had a hard time deadline and the current Pages workflow was already in place
Implication: READiscover launches first as a subpath deployment and can migrate later to the custom domain
Author: MH

Decision: Use environment-driven GA4 integration rather than hardcoding analytics in index.html
Reason: The app already uses Vite env variables and runtime analytics injection
Implication: Analytics only runs when VITE_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID is present at build time and can be cleanly disabled otherwise
Author: MH

Decision: Keep READiscover branded away from AI positioning
Reason: The product is a storytelling/media format and AI branding would misframe it publicly
Implication: Avoid .ai domain choices and treat AI as optional internal tooling rather than front-facing identity
Author: MH

Decision: Use publication-first strategy rather than trying to become a platform immediately
Reason: Limited resources and need to prove the format before scaling to outside creators
Implication: Focus remains on flagship stories and repeatable editorial system before creator tooling or marketplace ambitions
Author: MH

Decision: Adopt 3-layer media signaling system
Reason: Users were not clearly realizing when segments contained playback-cued media or when media was about to appear
Implication: READiscover will signal media at the segment layer, timeline layer, and active cue layer
Author: MH

Decision: Use vertical segment-level media indicators instead of inline prose icons
Reason: Inline icons could interrupt reading flow, while a structural rail preserves story-first layout
Implication: Segments with media will show gold iconographic markers attached to the segment structure
Author: MH

Decision: Add clickable media markers to playback progress bar
Reason: Users need to see that media moments are coming and should be able to jump directly to them
Implication: Progress bar becomes both transport control and media anticipation layer
Author: MH

Decision: Use tasteful active-cue interruption when media fires
Reason: Media currently risks appearing too quietly and being missed by users
Implication: Active media cues will trigger subtle state shift, entrance animation, and temporary explanatory label
Author: MH

Decision: Support GIFs as first-class READiscover media cues
Reason: GIFs and memes may strengthen voice, pacing, branding, and cultural/contextual storytelling
Implication: Media cue system should handle GIFs alongside charts, images, and other visual assets
Author: MH

Decision: Prioritize mobile media presence and discoverability before CMS or word-level sync
Reason: Current biggest product risk is users not realizing how rich the experience is early enough
Implication: Next development phase focuses on media signaling and mobile clarity rather than new authoring tools
Author: MH

Decision: Defer mobile overlay redesign until media signaling system is tested
Reason: Overlay behavior depends on knowing how segment icons, progress markers, and cue activation work together
Implication: Mobile layout changes will be evaluated after first three media-discovery layers are implemented
Author: MH

Decision: Defer word-level playback UI while preserving it as long-term goal
Reason: Word-level sync remains important but could distract from immediate clarity and discoverability work
Implication: V2 refinement will not implement word-level highlighting yet, but future architecture should avoid blocking it
Author: MH

Decision: Add tutorial-only visual demos for unavailable interactive states
Reason: Tutorial steps were pointing to empty or inactive UI when the real feature surfaces were not available yet
Implication: Tutorial can teach text/media/inspect concepts without mutating playback or story state
Author: MH

Decision: Route pointer-activated controls back toward playback keyboard behavior
Reason: Spacebar could re-trigger focused buttons or scroll the page instead of toggling playback
Implication: Normal playback interaction keeps Space as a playback shortcut unless typing or intentionally keyboard-focused
Author: MH

Decision: Allow mobile media peeks to reappear on replay or seek
Reason: Mobile previews felt buggy because they appeared once and were permanently suppressed
Implication: Users can revisit media cues and still receive the intended visual signal
Author: MH

Decision: Add visible affordance to media progress markers
Reason: Clickable gold dots worked but did not clearly communicate their purpose
Implication: Progress markers now better signal synced media jump points through labels, states, and expanded-control hints
Author: MH

Decision: Rename vague playback and media actions
Reason: User-facing labels like Open and Inspect reflected implementation concepts more than user intent
Implication: Controls and media actions now use clearer language such as Controls, View chart, View media, and Visual cue
Author: MH

Decision: Group segment rail media indicators by type and continuation context
Reason: Per-segment markers created clutter and failed to represent media attached to continuation segments
Implication: Media rails now better summarize media presence across connected preview segments while reducing duplicated indicators
Author: MH

Decision: Normalize legacy inline media behavior with timeline media cues
Reason: Older hyperlinked GIF/image interactions could linger or conflict with active playback-cued media
Implication: Inline media now participates more consistently in the active media priority model
Author: MH

Decision: Add dev-only media debug HUD
Reason: Manual UX review needed reliable visibility into playback time, active segment, active cue, and upcoming cue state
Implication: Reviewers can use ?debug=media to capture and debug temporal media behavior without mutating story state
Author: MH

Decision: Defer hero-area media cue demonstration
Reason: Review found that sync is not obvious until body text, but this pass focused on urgent tutorial/media/control fixes
Implication: Hero or pre-body media cue strategy remains open for a future first-minute experience pass
Author: MH

Decision: Defer full playback control redesign
Reason: Immediate label improvements helped but the expanded playback panel still needs a dedicated clarity pass
Implication: Transport controls remain functional while broader player information architecture is handled separately
Author: MH

Decision: Plan a future Context Layer for people characters sources glossary notes and other lightweight references
Reason: READiscover can add value across journalism fiction poetry podcasting and branded media by surfacing quick context without forcing users to leave the story
Implication: Future media/context architecture should distinguish story-native media from lightweight context cards and support optional mention-triggered previews later in the roadmap
Author: MH

Decision: Distinguish story-native media context cards source cards and sponsored media as separate future layers
Reason: Charts GIFs citations biographies and ads serve different purposes and should not share the same visual or interaction treatment
Implication: READiscover’s future media model should support layer or intent metadata so each kind of companion object can be displayed with appropriate priority and visual weight
Author: MH

Decision: Add dedicated Codebase Tutor agent for explanatory documentation
Reason: The project owner needs to understand and maintain a growing AI-assisted codebase without relying on sparse or overly technical comments
Implication: A recurring documentation agent will add generous plain-English comments and architecture notes for significant files while avoiding behavior changes and unnecessary line-by-line noise
Author: MH

Decision: Make mini-player progress track section-local
Reason: Filtering media markers to the current preview while keeping the track scaled to the full story created a misleading mostly empty progress bar
Implication: The mini-player timeline should use the same current-section scope as its visible media markers, while expanded controls can preserve full-story navigation
Author: MH

Decision: Plan future distinction between story-native media, source previews, utility context, and sponsored media
Reason: External source previews and ads could add credibility and monetization but may distract from story flow if treated like native media
Implication: Future media cue architecture should support distinct layers or intents without implementing source previews or ads in the current prototype
Author: MH

Decision: Increase prominence of section-scoped mini-player media markers
Reason: After switching the mini-player timeline to current-section scope, the small number of remaining cue markers can be made more visible without cluttering the player
Implication: Section-local media indicators should become larger, more legible, and easier to tap while remaining visually distinct from the playhead
Author: MH

Decision: Add always-visible previous/next section controls to the mini-player
Reason: Users may not clearly realize READiscover can be browsed chapter-by-chapter and not only through linear playback or scrubbing
Implication: The compact mini-player should expose logical section navigation directly, with previous/next controls that move between team previews rather than raw audio clips
Author: MH

Decision: Reframe audio as major but optional in READiscover
Reason: Current prototype shows that timed playback, text progression, and media choreography can create value even without narration
Implication: READiscover should be treated as a timeline-driven storytelling medium where audio is one powerful mode rather than a required foundation
Author: MH

Decision: Adopt playback-directed reading as the deeper product principle
Reason: The original audio-synced reading concept has evolved into a broader system where timeline state can guide text, media, charts, and context with or without audio
Implication: Product language and future schema should emphasize playable/timeline-driven reading rather than audio-first articles
Author: MH

Decision: Position READiscovermedia.com as a simple landing page before full platform launch
Reason: The custom domain should explain the medium and feature demos without forcing premature CMS, accounts, subscriptions, or revenue infrastructure
Implication: Initial READiscovermedia.com should focus on positioning, demo links, creator collaboration, and roadmap language
Author: MH

Decision: Adopt reading revival platform language for public positioning
Reason: The 2016 dossier framed READiscover as a way to preserve and reinvent reading in a media environment dominated by more sensory formats
Implication: Public messaging should center playable reading, written stories that move, and the Story Theater rather than generic immersive storytelling
Author: MH

Decision: Keep AI assistive rather than authorial in READiscover positioning
Reason: AI can help with timing, media suggestions, context cards, accessibility, and CMS workflows but should not displace the writer’s authority or become the product identity
Implication: READiscover should be publicly positioned as a storytelling medium while AI remains optional creator infrastructure
Author: MH

Decision: Use existing repeatability architecture rather than rebuilding multi-story foundation
Reason: Codex already added story registry, packaged story structure, slug routes, default story handling, and add-a-new-story documentation
Implication: Next story work should validate the architecture with a real second story instead of repeating foundational routing/registry work
Author: MH

Decision: Use Wolves-Nuggets reaction as first second-story test of repeatable architecture
Reason: The repeatability pass needs to be validated with a real standalone story that differs from the flagship playoff preview
Implication: A new Wolves reaction story should be its own READiscover story package rather than merged into the playoff preview or launched first on READiscovermedia.com
Author: MH

Decision: Host the Wolves-Nuggets reaction first on existing GH Pages/Hanson Hoops READiscover path
Reason: The current deployment surface is already working while READiscovermedia.com is not yet built
Implication: The second story should launch as a standalone GitHub Pages READiscover route and later be featured or mirrored from READiscovermedia.com
Author: MH

Decision: Finish a buildable story draft before tasking Codex with the second-story package
Reason: READiscover story structure depends on text order, section breaks, pacing, cue moments, and media placement
Implication: Codex should receive a solid draft and media cue map rather than inventing placeholder story structure too early
Author: MH

Decision: Reuse relevant Timberwolves preview media in the Wolves-Nuggets reaction story
Reason: Original preview media remains relevant and the first demo had limited exposure, making reuse efficient and editorially defensible
Implication: The second story can test repeatability by reusing existing GIFs/charts while adding only 1-2 new or replacement charts as needed
Author: MH

Decision: Use the Wolves-Nuggets reaction to test shorter personal essay mode
Reason: The flagship playoff preview is long, multi-section, and chart-heavy; the format also needs to prove itself on shorter emotional/editorial pieces
Implication: The Wolves story should test READiscover as a personal sports essay with lighter media density and possibly audio-optional playback
Author: MH

Decision: Explore Mobile Theater Mode as an alternative to scroll-first mobile reading
Reason: Current mobile layout still feels too much like a cluttered article page with playback controls layered on top
Implication: READiscover should test a mobile-specific split/focus mode that centers the currently playing text and current media while preserving full-scroll reading as an option
Author: MH

Decision: Keep companion media stage populated with meaningful resting content
Reason: Blank gaps between active media cues make the media system feel inactive or unfinished, especially on mobile
Implication: When no active cue is present, the media area should fall back to section identity, upcoming context, or story atmosphere rather than empty space
Author: MH

Decision: Plan three mobile focus levels for READiscover
Reason: Mobile needs a native interaction model that lets users move between immersive playback and traditional skimming without abandoning either experience
Implication: READiscover should explore Theater, Focus/Hybrid, and Read modes, with pinch gestures changing focus level and visible controls as fallback navigation
Author: MH

Decision: Treat pinch gestures as focus-mode controls rather than browser zoom
Reason: Mobile READiscover can use familiar pinch metaphors to change the scope of the story experience instead of merely scaling text
Implication: Pinch in/out should eventually transition between Theater, Focus/Hybrid, and Read modes while playback continues unless inspect mode is opened
Author: MH

Decision: Preserve full-scroll reading alongside future Mobile Theater Mode
Reason: Some users need skimming, searching, and traditional article navigation even if Theater Mode becomes the richer playback experience
Implication: Mobile redesign should add a focused playback mode without eliminating conventional read mode
Author: MH

Decision: Default to fresh Codex threads for each coherent implementation pass
Reason: Long Codex threads can accumulate stale context and encourage changes outside the intended scope
Implication: Use one Codex thread per focused work unit, with same-thread follow-up only for immediate fixes to that work
Author: MH

Decision: Use planning thread → Codex pass → triage/decision log loop for READiscover development
Reason: The project is increasingly agentic and needs a stable operating rhythm to avoid losing product coherence
Implication: Continue using this thread for strategy, fresh Codex threads for scoped implementation, and Sheets/docs for institutional memory
Author: MH

Decision: Plan Story Theater as named product concept for READiscovermedia.com
Reason: The Story Theater language ties the current product to the 2016 dossier and explains the playback/media experience better than generic article language
Implication: Site copy and product docs should consistently use Story Theater for the core playable reading environment
Author: MH

Decision: Add optional context layer language to READiscovermedia.com roadmap
Reason: Context cards, source previews, people/character cards, and glossary notes are emerging as important future differentiators
Implication: The landing page can mention context layers lightly as future-facing capability without promising implementation in the current prototype
Author: MH

Decision: Use one flagship story plus one shorter second story before prioritizing full READiscovermedia.com launch
Reason: A single demo is useful but a second story proves the format is repeatable across modes and tones
Implication: READiscovermedia.com becomes more credible once it can point to both the NBA preview and a second standalone story
Author: MH
